It appears at the very threshold of the Gospel narrative: Jesus is born 'in Bethlehem of Judea' (Matt 2:1, 5), John baptizes 'in the wilderness of Judea' (Matt 3:1), and crowds stream from Judea to hear Jesus (Matt 4:25; Mark 3:7-8). In Acts, Judea becomes the staging ground for the church's expansion outward: 'you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth' (Acts 1:8). The translations uniformly render it: Spanish 'Judea,' French 'Judee,' German 'Judäa.'"
